TASK ID: clique-to-vertex-cover

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Clique and TARGET is Vertex Cover. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = Clique
Clique.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a clique of AT LEAST k vertices: k vertices with an
edge between every two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k = 1 is yes whenever n >= 1. k > n is
always no.

TARGET = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-a75p487f

    reduce(instance) -> instance

The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

function.arguments:
{"command":"cat <<'EOF' > reduce.py
"""Reduction from Clique to Vertex Cover.

Given a Clique instance (n, edges, k), we construct a VertexCover instance
on the complement graph with parameter k' = n - k.  It is well‑known that
G has a clique of size at least k iff the complement graph \bar G has an
independent set of size at least k, which is equivalent to a vertex cover of
size at most n‑k.

The reduction runs in O(n^2) time, which is polynomial.
"""

def reduce(instance):
    """Transform a Clique instance into a VertexCover instance.

    Parameters
    ----------
    instance: dict
        A dictionary with keys "n", "edges", and "k" describing a graph for
        the Clique problem.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A dictionary suitable for the VertexCover problem.
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    k = instance["k"]
    # Build a set of existing edges for O(1) lookup. Store each edge as a tuple (u, v) with u < v.
    edge_set = set()
    for u, v in instance.get("edges", []):
        if u > v:
            u, v = v, u
        edge_set.add((u, v))
    # Complement edges: all unordered pairs not present in edge_set.
    complement_edges = []
    for u in range(n):
        for v in range(u + 1, n):
            if (u, v) not in edge_set:
                complement_edges.append([u, v])
    # New parameter for VertexCover.
    new_k = n - k
    return {"n": n, "edges": complement_edges, "k": new_k}

# The module may be imported by the evaluation harness; expose the function.
__all__ = ["reduce"]
EOF"}
